4 اعبد as trans.: see 2, former half, in four places. ＝
-A2- اعبدوا They collected themselves together; assembled together. (K.) ―
-b2- اعبد القَوْمُ بِالرَّجُلِ The people, or party, beat the man: (O, K:) or collected themselves together and beat him. (TA.) ＝
-A3- أُعْبِدَ بِهِ His riding-camel became fatigued: (S, O, K:) or perished; or flagged, or became powerless; or stopped with him: (S, O:) or died, or became ill, or went away, so that he was obliged to stop: (L:) i. q. أُبْدِعَ بِهِ [q. v.], (S, O, L, K,) from which it is formed by transposition. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
